claim: Vanna grounds text-to-SQL via a RAG model trained on DDL, documentation, and example SQL queries, retrieving the most relevant training items into the prompt at query time.
quote: train a RAG "model" on your data, and then ask questions which will return SQL queries

claim: Vanna's training accepts DDL statements (vn.train(ddl=...)), business documentation, and SQL queries, and retrieves the 10 most relevant training pieces per question to build the LLM prompt.
quote: Vanna will retrieve 10 most relevant pieces of training data and use it as part of the LLM prompt to generate the SQL.

claim: WrenAI is an open context layer (15.5k+ GitHub stars) that encodes schema, metrics, and relationships into Modeling Definition Language (MDL) to give LLM agents grounded, governed SQL across 20+ data sources.
quote: open context layer that gives AI agents grounded, governed memory, context, SQL across 20+ data sources

claim: Wren AI's MDL defines entities mapped to tables/columns, metrics, dimensions, filters and transformations so business meaning (e.g. 'total sales') is defined once and reused rather than re-inferred per query.
quote: the meaning of 'total sales'... is defined once and reused

claim: Dataherald (3.6k stars) is an agentic text-to-SQL engine that grounds via schema tools, a Context Store of business/data logic, and a GetFewShotExamples tool that dynamically retrieves golden Question/SQL pairs.
quote: GetFewShotExamples tool... allowing the agent to request relevant Question/SQL pairs dynamically

claim: LlamaIndex NLSQLTableQueryEngine injects table schema context into the prompt; for many tables it uses SQLTableNodeMapping to index per-table schemas (ObjectIndex) and retrieve only relevant tables to avoid context overflow.
quote: if the total size of table schemas overflows your context window, you can store the table schema in an index using the SQLTableNodeMapping object

claim: LlamaIndex (50k+ stars) provides NLSQLRetriever and NLSQLQueryEngine components that retrieve table schemas plus sample rows to improve SQL generation accuracy.
quote: NLSQLRetriever and NLSQLQueryEngine components, retrieving table schemas, contextual structure overviews, and actual data rows

claim: LangChain (138k+ stars) provides SQLDatabase/SQLDatabaseChain utilities but requires careful prompt engineering and schema filtering for large databases.
quote: LangChain excels at building production-ready applications but requires careful prompt engineering and schema filtering for large databases

claim: DAIL-SQL (635 stars) is a few-shot NL2SQL method reaching 86.6% execution accuracy by combining Code Representation prompts (full schema with PK/FK) and DAIL example selection that masks domain words and ranks by question+query similarity.
quote: A efficient and effective few-shot NL2SQL method on GPT-4.

claim: DAIL-SQL's question representation uses Code Representation Prompt because it contains full database information including primary and foreign keys, and DAIL_S selects examples by masking domain-specific words and ranking by embedding distance plus query similarity.
quote: DAIL-SQL adopts Code Representation Prompt (CR_P)... it contains full information of the database, including primary and foreign keys

claim: Snowflake Cortex Analyst grounds text-to-SQL on a YAML semantic model defining logical tables, dimensions, facts, metrics, relationships, synonyms, and verified queries, because raw schemas lack business definitions and metric handling.
quote: Generic AI solutions often struggle with text-to-SQL conversions when given only a database schema, as schemas lack critical knowledge like business process definitions and metrics handling.

claim: Databricks Genie grounds on Unity Catalog metadata (table/column descriptions, RLS policies), while BigQuery Gemini reads Dataform-defined views plus Information Schema; Cortex Analyst ships its own YAML semantic model.
quote: Reads metadata from Unity Catalog (table descriptions, column comments, row-level security policies)

claim: The dbt Semantic Layer reports 83% NL-query accuracy when grounding text-to-SQL on its metrics/dimensions/entities ontology versus ~40% for LLMs writing raw SQL against undecorated tables.
quote: 83% accuracy on natural language queries when backed by the semantic layer, compared to approximately 40% accuracy when LLMs write raw SQL against undecorated tables

claim: The Open Semantic Interchange (OSI), released January 2026, is a vendor-neutral YAML standard for semantic metadata backed by Snowflake, dbt Labs, Cube, Databricks, AtScale and 40+ partners, aimed at portable LLM grounding.
quote: Open Semantic Interchange specification, released in January 2026, is a vendor-neutral, YAML-based standard for representing semantic metadata
